page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-2 is an x86_64 architecture instance within the E2 server family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon core with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations indicate modest compute and memory performance. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance score is 1101.98, and the multi-core score is 1451.88, placing both in the lower performance tiers. Memory bandwidth tests show 80.53 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 12.0 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Cryptographic and integer operations are supported via hardware flags such as AES, BMI2, and FMA, though overall PassMark CPU and memory scores remain in the bottom quartile.

From a resource density perspective, the e2-highmem-2 offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads requiring higher memory capacity relative to compute power. Due to its lower CPU performance and lack of local storage, it is not suited for high-performance computing, large-scale databases, or intensive data processing. Instead, it is best aligned with lightweight memory-bound applications, small Redis caching layers, basic web serving, or small-scale text processing tasks.
